microtheory.name: music_theory
microtheory.definition: Formal organization of pitch + rhythm + harmony in music. Scales, modes, chord progressions, voice leading, counterpoint, form. The structural grammar underlying Western (and other) music traditions. Substrate analogue: hierarchical pattern grammar over substrate's pitch + timing representations.

concepts.name: major_scale
concepts.definition: Whole-whole-half-whole-whole-whole-half intervals. C-D-E-F-G-A-B. Foundation of Western tonality. Substrate analogue: substrate's most-common pitch template.

concepts.name: minor_scale
concepts.definition: Whole-half-whole-whole-half-whole-whole. Natural, harmonic, melodic variants. Substrate analogue: substrate's secondary pitch template.

concepts.name: pentatonic_scale
concepts.definition: 5 pitches per octave. Major (C-D-E-G-A) + minor variants. Foundation of many traditions; emotionally neutral. Substrate analogue: substrate's universal scale prior.

concepts.name: chromatic_scale
concepts.definition: All 12 semitones in succession. Substrate analogue: substrate's exhaustive pitch enumeration.

concepts.name: whole_tone_scale
concepts.definition: Six pitches in whole-tone steps. Impressionist + jazz. Substrate analogue: substrate's symmetric scale prior.

concepts.name: modes
concepts.definition: Ionian (major), Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian (natural minor), Locrian. Different starting points of major scale. Substrate analogue: substrate's contextual scale prior.

concepts.name: interval_types
concepts.definition: Perfect (unison, 4th, 5th, octave), major/minor (2nd, 3rd, 6th, 7th), augmented, diminished. Substrate analogue: substrate's relational pitch concepts.

concepts.name: consonant_intervals
concepts.definition: Octave + perfect 5th + perfect 4th + major/minor 3rd + 6th. Stable, resolved. Substrate analogue: substrate's low-frustration multi-pitch states.

concepts.name: dissonant_intervals
concepts.definition: Major/minor 2nd + 7th + tritone (augmented 4th). Unstable, demanding resolution. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-frustration multi-pitch states.

concepts.name: tritone
concepts.definition: Augmented 4th / diminished 5th. Six semitones. Highest tension. 'Devil in music' in medieval times. Substrate analogue: substrate's maximally-frustrated dyad.

concepts.name: triad
concepts.definition: Three-note chord. Major (1-3-5), minor (1-♭3-5), augmented (1-3-#5), diminished (1-♭3-♭5). Substrate analogue: substrate's basic harmonic primitive.

concepts.name: seventh_chord
concepts.definition: Triad + 7th. Major7, minor7, dominant7, diminished7, half-diminished. Substrate analogue: substrate's extended harmonic state.

concepts.name: chord_inversion
concepts.definition: Same chord with different bass note. Root position vs first/second/third inversion. Substrate analogue: substrate's harmonic-class-with-bass-permutation.

concepts.name: voicing
concepts.definition: How chord pitches are distributed across registers + instruments. Substrate analogue: substrate's chord-state spatial pattern.

concepts.name: extended_chord
concepts.definition: 9th, 11th, 13th chords. Adds color tones above the 7th. Jazz vocabulary. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-dimensional harmonic state.

concepts.name: tonic
concepts.definition: First scale degree; home pitch. Resolution point. Substrate analogue: substrate's central basin attractor.

concepts.name: dominant
concepts.definition: Fifth scale degree. Drives toward tonic. V→I cadence. Substrate analogue: substrate's expectation-buildup state.

concepts.name: subdominant
concepts.definition: Fourth scale degree. Pre-dominant — predecessor in IV→V→I. Substrate analogue: substrate's harmonic-prep state.

concepts.name: leading_tone
concepts.definition: Seventh scale degree, half-step below tonic. Pulls strongly to tonic. Substrate analogue: substrate's maximum-tension-to-tonic state.

concepts.name: tonal_hierarchy
concepts.definition: Krumhansl 1990. Within a key: tonic > dominant > mediant > others. Listener-learned. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-key probability distribution over pitch classes.

concepts.name: cadence
concepts.definition: Harmonic + melodic formula closing a phrase. Authentic (V-I), plagal (IV-I), half (X-V), deceptive (V-vi). Substrate analogue: substrate's expected phrase-ending pattern.

concepts.name: chord_progression
concepts.definition: Sequence of chords forming harmonic motion. I-IV-V-I; ii-V-I; pop progressions. Substrate analogue: substrate's harmonic-state-sequence template.

concepts.name: voice_leading
concepts.definition: How individual lines move between chords. Smooth voice leading minimizes motion + avoids parallel 5ths/octaves. Substrate analogue: substrate's minimum-change harmonic transition.

concepts.name: modulation
concepts.definition: Movement from one key to another. Through pivot chord, common tone, or direct. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-attractor handoff.

concepts.name: secondary_dominant
concepts.definition: V of X — temporary dominant pulling toward a non-tonic chord. Tonicization. Substrate analogue: substrate's local-attractor formation within a larger basin.

concepts.name: counterpoint_species
concepts.definition: Fux 1725. 1st = note-against-note, 2nd = 2:1, 3rd = 4:1, 4th = syncopation, 5th = florid. Bach's mastery. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel pattern grammar.

concepts.name: fugue
concepts.definition: Imitative counterpoint. Subject + answer + countersubject + episodes + development. Substrate analogue: substrate's pattern-transformation grammar.

concepts.name: invertible_counterpoint
concepts.definition: Lines that work whether one is above or below the other. Substrate analogue: substrate's voice-symmetric harmonic relations.

concepts.name: form
concepts.definition: Large-scale structural organization. Binary, ternary, rondo, sonata, theme-and-variations. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical temporal segmentation.

concepts.name: sonata_form
concepts.definition: Exposition + development + recapitulation. Classical period dominant form. Substrate analogue: substrate's statement-conflict-resolution narrative structure.

concepts.name: song_form
concepts.definition: Verse + chorus + bridge variants. AABA, ABABCB. Substrate analogue: substrate's repetition-with-variation grammar.

rules.name: tonal_hierarchy_predicts_pitch_expectation
rules.head: the substrate hears music in a key
rules.body: the next pitch is more likely tonic + dominant than dissonant pitches. Krumhansl 1990 — substrate's key-conditioned pitch prior.

rules.name: cadences_close_phrases_via_resolution
rules.head: the substrate hears a chord progression building tension
rules.body: an authentic cadence (V-I) resolves the tension; substrate's harmonic-completion mechanism. Half-cadences leave it open.

rules.name: voice_leading_prefers_minimum_motion
rules.head: the substrate processes a chord-to-chord transition
rules.body: smooth voice leading (small intervals, common tones held) is perceived as natural; large jumps + parallel 5ths/octaves are perceived as primitive. Substrate's optimal transition is minimum-change.

rules.name: consonance_dissonance_drives_harmonic_progression
rules.head: the substrate hears a dissonant chord
rules.body: it expects resolution to consonance. Resolution + delay create musical narrative. Substrate's harmonic expectation = consonance-seeking.

rules.name: modulation_shifts_basin_to_new_key
rules.head: the substrate's tonal-hierarchy basin matches one key
rules.body: modulation moves it to a new basin via shared chord (pivot) or direct shift. Substrate's basin-attractor handoff under harmonic context change.

rules.name: form_organizes_at_multiple_scales
rules.head: the substrate processes an extended musical work
rules.body: it tracks structure at note/beat/phrase/section/movement levels simultaneously. Hierarchical segmentation. Substrate's multi-scale temporal pattern recognition.
